title: Redox and Electrochemistry: Batteries

cards.b: Rust, a burning candle, your phone battery and the aluminium in a foil roll are all redox chemistry: electrons transferred from one species to another. Harness that flow and you have a battery. Force it backwards with electricity and you can extract metals.

OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons; Reduction Is Gain.

Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu. Zinc loses 2 electrons (oxidised), copper ions gain them (reduced). The zinc is the reducing agent; Cu2+ is the oxidising agent. The two halves always occur together.

Oxidation numbers track the shift. In Zn, it goes 0 to +2; in Cu2+ it goes +2 to 0.

We split each redox reaction in two.

  • Oxidation: Zn → Zn2+ + 2e-
  • Reduction: Cu2+ + 2e- → Cu

Add them so electrons cancel. This also helps balance difficult equations.

Alessandro Volta (1800) built the first battery (the voltaic pile). John Daniell (1836) made a steadier zinc-copper cell. Put each metal in a solution of its own ions, connect with a wire and a salt bridge.

Anode = oxidation; cathode = reduction. Electrons flow from anode to cathode.

Each half-cell has a standard potential. Zn2+/Zn is -0.76 V and Cu2+/Cu is +0.34 V. Cell voltage = E(cathode) - E(anode) = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V.

More positive potential means a stronger tendency to be reduced. This ranks metals: reactive metals (Li, Na, Zn) sit at negative values.

Electrolysis uses electricity to force a non-spontaneous reaction. Michael Faraday (1834) showed the amount of product is proportional to the charge passed. Uses: extracting aluminium (Hall-Héroult, 1886), electroplating, splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen.

Lithium-ion batteries: Li+ ions shuttle between electrodes. The 2019 Chemistry Nobel went to Goodenough, Whittingham and Yoshino for them. Fuel cells combine H2 and O2 to make water and electricity.

Oxidation number of Mn in KMnO4: K is +1, four O is -8, so Mn = +7.

Faraday's idea: charge of 1 mole of electrons = 96,500 C. To deposit 1 mol of copper (Cu2+ needs 2 e-), you need 2 x 96,500 = 193,000 C. At 10 A, time = 193,000 / 10 = 19,300 s, about 5.4 hours.

• Oxidation does not always involve oxygen. It is electron loss.
  • Electrons do not travel through the salt bridge. Ions do, to keep the charge balanced.
  • Rusting is redox. 4Fe + 3O2 + water → Fe2O3 (hydrated rust).
  • Anode sign differs. It is negative in a galvanic cell and positive in electrolysis; it is always where oxidation occurs.

cards.h: Delhi iron pillar and India's battery push
cards.b:
The Delhi iron pillar (about 1,600 years old, about 7 m tall) has barely rusted. Studies by metallurgists, including R. Balasubramaniam at IIT Kanpur, link this to its high phosphorus content, which helped form a thin, protective layer of iron hydrogen phosphate. That is redox chemistry in practice.

India's 2021 PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries aims for 50 GWh of domestic capacity.

• Oxidation = loss of electrons; reduction = gain.
  • Galvanic cells turn chemical energy into electricity; E(cell) = E(cathode) - E(anode).
  • Electrolysis forces reactions with electricity.
